description:
Erection of a single-storey rear infil brick extension, replace non-original timber sash windows with timber sash windows, alteration to window opening at lower ground floor level to modern rear extension to take new aluminium framed glazed door.
Replace artificial slate to front pitch with natural slate; replace existing velux rooflights to front and rear pitched roofs with conservation rooflights; reinstate decorative gable to front elevation to match original with integrated swift brick; reinstate copings to front gable; replace upvc drainage goods with cast iron. Remove non-original cast iron pot guards to front and rear. 
Helical bar repair to brickwork; lime repointing. 
To front garden relay drainage with new manholes; lift and relay york stone paving; new timber bin store; repair stone front steps. Replace modern railings and gate with cast iron railings and gate on new stone coping. Raise brick piers and replace caps with cast stone to match original. Repair railings to side boundaries. 
To rear garden: new bike store; new ASHP, new stone paving to side passage.
decision_conditions: <p>Any new plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise sensitive premises. REASON: To ensure that the occupiers and users of the proposed development do not suffer a loss of amenity by reason of excess environmental noise.</p>

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<div>All new works and works of making good to the retained fabric, whether internal or external, shall be finished to match the original work with regard to the methods used and to material, dimensions, composition, form, colour, finish and profile unless otherwise specified in the details hereby approved.&nbsp;</div><div><br></div><div>REASON: In order to protect the special interest of the listed building.&nbsp;</div><div><br></div>

<p>Tree Protection Compliance (ASHP Installation)The installation of the Air Source Heat Pump (ASHP) and all associated infrastructure hereby permitted shall be carried out in strict accordance with the details indicated on the approved Site Block Plan (Drawing No. DBV25/SPP/001/F) and the following arboricultural protection measures:Above-Ground Pipework: All pipework connecting the ASHP to the dwelling that falls within the Root Protection Area (RPA) of the mature Beech tree (T6) shall be installed entirely above ground.Restricted Trenching: Any subterranean trenching required for insulated pipework shall be located strictly outside the bounds of the Beech tree's (T6) Root Protection Area.'No-Dig' Foundation: The base/plinth for the ASHP unit shall be constructed using a strictly 'no-dig' methodology (such as a cellular confinement system or resting directly on the existing soil grade) to ensure zero excavation or root severance occurs within the RPA.Manual Installation: All works within the RPA, including the siting of the ASHP and the laying of above-ground pipework, shall be undertaken manually using hand tools only. No heavy machinery shall be tracked across the unprotected soil within the RPA.The installed system and protective measures shall be retained as such thereafter.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To ensure the works are carried out in a manner that safeguards the health, structural stability, and longevity of the mature Beech tree (T6) during and after installation, preserving its amenity value to the site and surrounding conservation area, in accordance with Policy LP51 in the Local Plan 2033 (adopted 2020) regarding tree protection.<br></p><div><br></div>

The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

<p>&nbsp;Tree and ground protection for all retained trees at the site shall be undertaken in accordance with BS5837:2012 (Trees in relation to construction - Recommendations) and will protect the Root Protection Area (RPA) calculated as described in Table 2 of that British Standard for the duration of all site works (including demolition) undertaken in connection with the development hereby approved.</p><p>&nbsp;1. Protective Fencing</p><p>&nbsp;The protective fencing will be 2.4m high and conform to Figure 2 of BS5837:2012, i.e. a scaffold framework comprising a vertical and horizontal framework, well braced to resist impacts, with vertical tubes spaced at a maximum interval of 3m. On to this weldmesh panels should be securely fixed with wire or scaffold clamps. Suitable analogues such as boundary walls or fences may be acceptable if adequately robust.</p><p>&nbsp;2. Temporary Ground Protection within the RPA</p><p>&nbsp;Where construction access is required within the RPA, new temporary ground protection shall be implemented and maintained. This protection must be capable of supporting any traffic entering or using the site without being distorted or causing compaction of the underlying soil within the RPA. The ground protection used shall be selected based on the anticipated traffic loading:</p><p>&nbsp;a) For Pedestrian Movements Only: A single thickness of scaffold boards placed either on top of a driven scaffold frame, so as to form a suspended walkway, or on top of a compression-resistant layer (e.g., 100 mm depth of woodchip), laid onto a geotextile membrane.</p><p>&nbsp;b) For Pedestrian-Operated Plant (up to 2 t gross weight): Proprietary, inter-linked ground protection boards placed on top of a compression-resistant layer (e.g., 150 mm depth of woodchip), laid onto a geotextile membrane.</p><p>&nbsp;c) For Wheeled or Tracked Construction Traffic (exceeding 2 t gross weight): An alternative system (e.g., proprietary systems or pre-cast reinforced concrete slabs) to an engineering specification designed in conjunction with arboricultural advice, to accommodate the likely loading to which it will be subjected.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To comply with Section 197(a) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, and to ensure the long-term health and survival of retained trees by protecting their root systems from damage and soil compaction.<br></p><div><br></div>
